passages.text: Then Saul ordered his son Jonathan and all his servants to kill David. But Jonathan delighted greatly in David, so he warned David, saying, “My father Saul intends to kill you. Be on your guard in the morning; find a secret place and hide there.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul spoke to his son Jonathan.
Saul spoke to all his servants.
Saul ordered them to kill David.
Jonathan was Saul’s son.
Jonathan loved David very much.
Jonathan warned David.
Jonathan said, “My father Saul wants to kill you.”
Jonathan said, “Be careful in the morning.”
Jonathan said, “Go to a secret place.”
Jonathan said, “Hide there.”
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר שָׁא֗וּל אֶל־ יוֹנָתָ֤ן בְּנוֹ֙ וְאֶל־ כָּל־ עֲבָדָ֔יו לְהָמִ֖ית אֶת־ דָּוִ֑ד וִיהֽוֹנָתָן֙ בֶּן־ שָׁא֔וּל חָפֵ֥ץ בְּדָוִ֖ד מְאֹֽד׃ וַיַּגֵּ֤ד יְהוֹנָתָן֙ לְדָוִ֣ד לֵאמֹ֔ר מְבַקֵּ֛שׁ שָׁא֥וּל אָבִ֖י לַהֲמִיתֶ֑ךָ וְעַתָּה֙ הִשָּֽׁמֶר־ נָ֣א בַבֹּ֔קֶר וְיָשַׁבְתָּ֥ בַסֵּ֖תֶר וְנַחְבֵּֽאתָ׃

passages.text: I will go out and stand beside my father in the field where you are, so I can ask about you. And if I find out anything, I will tell you.”
passages.sermon:
Jonathan was Saul’s son.
Jonathan loved David very much.
Jonathan spoke to David.
Jonathan said, “I will go out.”
“I will stand beside my father Saul.”
“I will stand in the field where you are.”
“I will speak to my father about you.”
“I will see what happens.”
“I will tell you everything I find out.”
passages.original: וַאֲנִ֨י אֵצֵ֜א וְעָמַדְתִּ֣י לְיַד־ אָבִ֗י בַּשָּׂדֶה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתָּ֣ה שָׁ֔ם וַאֲנִ֕י אֲדַבֵּ֥ר בְּךָ֖ אֶל־ אָבִ֑י וְרָאִ֥יתִי מָ֖ה וְהִגַּ֥דְתִּי לָֽךְ׃ס

passages.text: Then Jonathan spoke well of David to his father Saul and said to him, “The king should not sin against his servant David; he has not sinned against you. In fact, his actions have been highly beneficial to you.
passages.sermon:
Jonathan was Saul’s son.
Jonathan spoke to his father Saul.
Jonathan spoke about David.
Jonathan said good things about David.
Jonathan said to Saul, “The king must not sin against David.”
David is your servant.
David has not sinned against you.
David’s actions have helped you very much.
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֨ר יְהוֹנָתָ֤ן בְּדָוִד֙ ט֔וֹב אֶל־ שָׁא֖וּל אָבִ֑יו וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵ֠לָיו אַל־ יֶחֱטָ֨א הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ בְּעַבְדּ֣וֹ בְדָוִ֗ד כִּ֣י ל֤וֹא חָטָא֙ לָ֔ךְ וְכִ֥י מַעֲשָׂ֖יו טוֹב־ לְךָ֥ מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: He took his life in his hands when he struck down the Philistine, and the LORD worked a great salvation for all Israel. You saw it and rejoiced, so why would you sin against innocent blood by killing David for no reason?”
passages.sermon:
David risked his life.
David fought the Philistine.
David killed the Philistine.
The LORD saved all Israel through this.
You saw what happened.
You rejoiced at the victory.
Do not sin by shedding innocent blood.
Do not kill David without cause.
passages.original: וַיָּשֶׂם֩ אֶת־ נַפְשׁ֨וֹ בְכַפּ֜וֹ וַיַּ֣ךְ אֶת־ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֗י וַיַּ֨עַשׂ יְהוָ֜ה תְּשׁוּעָ֤ה גְדוֹלָה֙ לְכָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל רָאִ֖יתָ וַתִּשְׂמָ֑ח וְלָ֤מָּה תֶֽחֱטָא֙ בְּדָ֣ם נָקִ֔י לְהָמִ֥ית אֶת־ דָּוִ֖ד חִנָּֽם׃

passages.text: Saul listened to the voice of Jonathan and swore an oath: “As surely as the LORD lives, David will not be put to death.”
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Jonathan was Saul’s son.
Jonathan spoke to Saul about David.
Saul listened to Jonathan’s words.
Saul made a promise.
Saul swore an oath.
Saul said, “As surely as the LORD lives, David will not die.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמַ֥ע שָׁא֖וּל בְּק֣וֹל יְהוֹנָתָ֑ן וַיִּשָּׁבַ֣ע שָׁא֔וּל חַי־ יְהוָ֖ה אִם־ יוּמָֽת׃

passages.text: So Jonathan summoned David and told him all these things. Then Jonathan brought David to Saul to serve him as he had before.
passages.sermon:
Jonathan was the son of Saul.
Jonathan called David.
Jonathan told David everything that had happened.
Jonathan brought David to Saul.
David stood before Saul as he had in the past.
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֤א יְהוֹנָתָן֙ לְדָוִ֔ד וַיַּגֶּד־ לוֹ֙ יְה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן אֵ֥ת כָּל־ הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיָּבֵ֨א יְהוֹנָתָ֤ן אֶת־ דָּוִד֙ אֶל־ שָׁא֔וּל וַיְהִ֥י לְפָנָ֖יו כְּאֶתְמ֥וֹל שִׁלְשֽׁוֹם׃ס

passages.text: When war broke out again, David went out and fought the Philistines and struck them with such a mighty blow that they fled before him.
passages.sermon:
War started again.
David went out to fight.
David fought against the Philistines.
David struck the Philistines with a great blow.
The Philistines ran away from David.
passages.original: וַתּ֥וֹסֶף הַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה לִֽהְי֑וֹת וַיֵּצֵ֨א דָוִ֜ד וַיִּלָּ֣חֶם בַּפְּלִשְׁתִּ֗ים וַיַּ֤ךְ בָּהֶם֙ מַכָּ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֔ה וַיָּנֻ֖סוּ מִפָּנָֽיו׃

passages.text: But as Saul was sitting in his house with his spear in his hand, a spirit of distress from the LORD came upon him. While David was playing the harp, Saul tried to pin him to the wall with his spear. But the spear struck the wall and David eluded him, ran away, and escaped that night.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul sat in his house.
He held a spear in his hand.
A harmful spirit from the LORD came upon Saul.
David was also there.
David played music with his hand.
Saul tried to strike David with the spear.
Saul wanted to pin David to the wall.
David escaped from Saul.
The spear hit the wall instead.
David ran away that night.
David got away safely.
passages.original: וַתְּהִי֩ ר֨וּחַ יְהוָ֤ה׀ רָעָה֙ אֶל־ שָׁא֔וּל וְהוּא֙ בְּבֵית֣וֹ יוֹשֵׁ֔ב וַחֲנִית֖וֹ בְּיָד֑וֹ וְדָוִ֖ד מְנַגֵּ֥ן בְּיָֽד׃ וַיְבַקֵּ֨שׁ שָׁא֜וּל לְהַכּ֤וֹת בַּֽחֲנִית֙ בְּדָוִ֣ד וּבַקִּ֔יר וַיִּפְטַר֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י שָׁא֔וּל וַיַּ֥ךְ אֶֽת־ הַחֲנִ֖ית בַּקִּ֑יר וְדָוִ֛ד נָ֥ס וַיִּמָּלֵ֖ט בַּלַּ֥יְלָה הֽוּא׃פ

passages.text: Then Saul sent messengers to David’s house to watch him and kill him in the morning. But David’s wife Michal warned him, “If you do not run for your life tonight, tomorrow you will be dead!”
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul wanted to kill David.
Saul sent messengers to David’s house.
The messengers watched David’s house.
The messengers planned to kill David in the morning.
Michal was David’s wife.
Michal warned David.
Michal said, “If you do not escape tonight, you will die tomorrow.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ שָׁא֨וּל מַלְאָכִ֜ים אֶל־ בֵּ֤ית דָּוִד֙ לְשָׁמְר֔וֹ וְלַהֲמִית֖וֹ בַּבֹּ֑קֶר וַתַּגֵּ֣ד לְדָוִ֗ד מִיכַ֤ל אִשְׁתּוֹ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אִם־ אֵ֨ינְךָ֜ מְמַלֵּ֤ט אֶֽת־ נַפְשְׁךָ֙ הַלַּ֔יְלָה מָחָ֖ר אַתָּ֥ה מוּמָֽת׃

passages.text: So Michal lowered David from the window, and he ran away and escaped.
passages.sermon:
Michal was David’s wife.
Michal helped David escape.
Michal lowered David through a window.
David left the house.
David ran away.
David escaped.
passages.original: וַתֹּ֧רֶד מִיכַ֛ל אֶת־ דָּוִ֖ד בְּעַ֣ד הַחַלּ֑וֹן וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ וַיִּבְרַ֖ח וַיִּמָּלֵֽט׃

passages.text: Then Michal took a household idol and laid it in the bed, placed some goat hair on its head, and covered it with a garment.
passages.sermon:
Michal was David’s wife.
Michal took a household idol.
She put the idol in the bed.
She took goat hair.
She put the goat hair at the head of the bed.
She covered the idol with a garment.
passages.original: וַתִּקַּ֨ח מִיכַ֜ל אֶת־ הַתְּרָפִ֗ים וַתָּ֙שֶׂם֙ אֶל־ הַמִּטָּ֔ה וְאֵת֙ כְּבִ֣יר הָֽעִזִּ֔ים שָׂ֖מָה מְרַֽאֲשֹׁתָ֑יו וַתְּכַ֖ס בַּבָּֽגֶד׃ס

passages.text: When Saul sent the messengers to seize David, Michal said, “He is ill.”
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul wanted to capture David.
Saul sent messengers to take David.
Michal was David’s wife.
Michal spoke to the messengers.
Michal said, “David is ill.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח שָׁא֛וּל מַלְאָכִ֖ים לָקַ֣חַת אֶת־ דָּוִ֑ד וַתֹּ֖אמֶר חֹלֶ֥ה הֽוּא׃פ

passages.text: But Saul sent the messengers back to see David and told them, “Bring him up to me in his bed so I can kill him.”
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul wanted to kill David.
Saul sent messengers to David’s house.
Saul told the messengers to look for David.
Saul said to the messengers, “Bring David to me.”
Saul said, “Bring him in his bed.”
Saul said, “I will kill him.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח שָׁאוּל֙ אֶת־ הַמַּלְאָכִ֔ים לִרְא֥וֹת אֶת־ דָּוִ֖ד לֵאמֹ֑ר הַעֲל֨וּ אֹת֧וֹ בַמִּטָּ֛ה אֵלַ֖י לַהֲמִתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: And when the messengers entered, there was the idol in the bed with the quilt of goats’ hair on its head.
passages.sermon:
Saul sent messengers to capture David.
The messengers entered David’s house.
They saw a bed.
An idol was in the bed.
A quilt made of goats’ hair was on the idol’s head.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ הַמַּלְאָכִ֔ים וְהִנֵּ֥ה הַתְּרָפִ֖ים אֶל־ הַמִּטָּ֑ה וּכְבִ֥יר הָעִזִּ֖ים מְרַאֲשֹׁתָֽיו׃

passages.text: And Saul said to Michal, “Why did you deceive me like this? You sent my enemy away and he has escaped!” Michal replied, “He said to me, ‘Help me get away, or I will kill you!’ ”
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Michal was Saul’s daughter.
David was Saul’s enemy.
Saul spoke to Michal.
Saul said, “Why did you deceive me?”
Saul said, “You sent my enemy away.”
Saul said, “He has escaped.”
Michal answered Saul.
Michal said, “He told me, ‘Let me go.’”
Michal said, “He said, ‘Why should I kill you?’”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שָׁא֜וּל אֶל־ מִיכַ֗ל לָ֤מָּה כָּ֙כָה֙ רִמִּיתִ֔נִי וַתְּשַׁלְּחִ֥י אֶת־ אֹיְבִ֖י וַיִּמָּלֵ֑ט וַתֹּ֤אמֶר מִיכַל֙ אֶל־ שָׁא֔וּל הוּא־ אָמַ֥ר אֵלַ֛י שַׁלְּחִ֖נִי לָמָ֥ה אֲמִיתֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: So David ran away and escaped. And he went to Samuel at Ramah and told him all that Saul had done to him. Then he and Samuel went to Naioth and stayed there.
passages.sermon:
David was in danger because Saul wanted to kill him.
David ran away from Saul.
David escaped safely.
David went to Samuel.
Samuel was at Ramah.
David told Samuel everything Saul had done to him.
David and Samuel left together.
David and Samuel went to Naioth.
David and Samuel stayed in Naioth.
passages.original: וְדָוִ֨ד בָּרַ֜ח וַיִּמָּלֵ֗ט וַיָּבֹ֤א אֶל־ שְׁמוּאֵל֙ הָרָמָ֔תָה וַיַּ֨גֶּד־ ל֔וֹ אֵ֛ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָֽשָׂה־ ל֖וֹ שָׁא֑וּל וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ הוּא֙ וּשְׁמוּאֵ֔ל וַיֵּשְׁב֖וּ בְּנֹוִית׃

passages.text: When Saul was told that David was at Naioth in Ramah, he sent messengers to capture him. But when they saw the group of prophets prophesying, with Samuel leading them, the Spirit of God came upon them, and Saul’s messengers also began to prophesy.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Someone told Saul, “David is at Naioth in Ramah.”
Saul wanted to capture David.
Saul sent messengers to take David.
The messengers arrived at Naioth.
They saw a group of prophets.
The prophets were prophesying.
Samuel was leading the prophets.
The Spirit of God came upon Saul’s messengers.
Saul’s messengers also began to prophesy.
passages.original: וַיֻּגַּ֥ד לְשָׁא֖וּל לֵאמֹ֑ר הִנֵּ֣ה דָוִ֔ד בְּנֹוִית בָּרָמָֽה׃ וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח שָׁא֣וּל מַלְאָכִים֮ לָקַ֣חַת אֶת־ דָּוִד֒ וַיַּ֗רְא אֶֽת־ לַהֲקַ֤ת הַנְּבִיאִים֙ נִבְּאִ֔ים וּשְׁמוּאֵ֕ל עֹמֵ֥ד נִצָּ֖ב עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וַתְּהִ֞י עַֽל־ מַלְאֲכֵ֤י שָׁאוּל֙ ר֣וּחַ אֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיִּֽתְנַבְּא֖וּ גַּם־ הֵֽמָּה׃

passages.text: When this was reported to Saul, he sent more messengers, but they began to prophesy as well. So Saul tried again and sent messengers a third time, and even they began to prophesy.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
People told Saul what happened.
Saul sent more messengers to capture David.
These messengers saw the prophets prophesying.
The Spirit of God came upon these messengers.
They also began to prophesy.
Saul sent messengers a third time.
The third group of messengers also began to prophesy.
passages.original: וַיַּגִּ֣דוּ לְשָׁא֗וּל וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ מַלְאָכִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים וַיִּֽתְנַבְּא֖וּ גַּם־ הֵ֑מָּה וַיֹּ֣סֶף שָׁא֗וּל וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ מַלְאָכִ֣ים שְׁלִשִׁ֔ים וַיִּֽתְנַבְּא֖וּ גַּם־ הֵֽמָּה׃

passages.text: Finally, Saul himself left for Ramah and came to the large cistern at Secu, where he asked, “Where are Samuel and David?” “At Naioth in Ramah,” he was told.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul left for Ramah.
He came to the large cistern at Secu.
Saul asked a question.
He said, “Where are Samuel and David?”
Someone answered Saul.
They said, “They are at Naioth in Ramah.”
passages.original: וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ גַּם־ ה֜וּא הָרָמָ֗תָה וַיָּבֹא֙ עַד־ בּ֤וֹר הַגָּדוֹל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּשֶּׂ֔כוּ וַיִּשְׁאַ֣ל וַיֹּ֔אמֶר אֵיפֹ֥ה שְׁמוּאֵ֖ל וְדָוִ֑ד וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הִנֵּ֖ה בְּנֹוִית בָּרָמָֽה׃

passages.text: So Saul went to Naioth in Ramah. But the Spirit of God came upon even Saul, and he walked along prophesying until he came to Naioth in Ramah.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul went to Naioth in Ramah.
The Spirit of God came upon Saul.
Saul began to prophesy as he walked.
Saul continued prophesying until he arrived at Naioth in Ramah.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ שָׁ֔ם אֶל־ נֹוִית בָּרָמָ֑ה וַתְּהִי֩ עָלָ֨יו גַּם־ ה֜וּא ר֣וּחַ אֱלֹהִ֗ים וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ הָלוֹךְ֙ וַיִּתְנַבֵּ֔א עַד־ בֹּא֖וֹ בְּנֹוִית בָּרָמָֽה׃

passages.text: Then Saul stripped off his robes and also prophesied before Samuel. And he collapsed and lay naked all that day and night. That is why it is said, “Is Saul also among the prophets?”
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul went to Naioth in Ramah.
The Spirit of God came upon Saul.
Saul took off his robes.
Saul prophesied before Samuel.
Saul fell down.
Saul lay naked all that day.
Saul lay naked all that night.
People saw what happened.
People said, “Is Saul also among the prophets?”
passages.original: וַיִּפְשַׁ֨ט גַּם־ ה֜וּא בְּגָדָ֗יו וַיִּתְנַבֵּ֤א גַם־ הוּא֙ לִפְנֵ֣י שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל וַיִּפֹּ֣ל עָרֹ֔ם כָּל־ הַיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא וְכָל־ הַלָּ֑יְלָה עַל־ כֵּן֙ יֹֽאמְר֔וּ הֲגַ֥ם שָׁא֖וּל בַּנְּבִיאִֽם׃פ
